def main():
    # 67 is prime, and a+b >= 2, so a+b must be 67 for (a+b) | 67.
    # Hence a+b <= 67, which bounds a and b to 1..66, so this search is exhaustive.
    LIMIT = 67
    solutions = []
    for a in range(1, LIMIT + 1):
        for b in range(1, LIMIT + 1):
            if a % (b + 1) == 0 and 67 % (a + b) == 0:
                solutions.append((a, b))

    all_a = sorted({a for a, _ in solutions})
    all_b = sorted({b for _, b in solutions})

    print("All solutions (a, b):", solutions)
    print("Possible a values:", all_a)
    print("Possible b values:", all_b)

    # Part (a): submitted a = 34
    claimed_a = 34
    a_ok = any(a == claimed_a for a, _ in solutions)
    print(f"Part (a) claimed a = {claimed_a}, witness b = "
          f"{[b for a, b in solutions if a == claimed_a]}")
    print("CHECK PASS (a)" if a_ok else "CHECK FAIL (a)")

    # Part (b): submitted reasoning concludes only (34, 33), so b-set = {33}
    claimed_b = {33}
    b_ok = set(all_b) == claimed_b
    print(f"Part (b) claimed b set = {sorted(claimed_b)}, "
          f"computed b set = {all_b}")
    print("CHECK PASS (b)" if b_ok else "CHECK FAIL (b)")

    # Verify each computed b explicitly with its witness a
    for a, b in solutions:
        ok = (a % (b + 1) == 0) and (67 % (a + b) == 0)
        print(f"  witness a={a}, b={b}: a%(b+1)={a % (b + 1)}, "
              f"67%(a+b)={67 % (a + b)} -> {'CHECK PASS' if ok else 'CHECK FAIL'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
